headline: Sony headphones can now be free PC head trackers for 200+ race & flight sims via open-source app
summary: An enthusiast-created open-source app, "Sony Head Tracker," leverages existing spatial audio sensors in compatible Sony headphones to provide real-time head tracking for PC games, enhancing immersion.
details: Developer Nicholas Slattery has created "Sony Head Tracker," an open-source app that transforms compatible Sony headphones and earbuds into real-time head trackers for PC games. This leverages the spatial audio sensors already present in many recent Sony models, which are typically limited to audio features.

The app acts as a bridge, tapping into Sony's Android Head Tracker protocol to read rotation vectors, gyroscope fields, and Euler Angles. This raw data is then streamed via UDP to OpenTrack software, which supports over 200 PC games.

Currently, Sony's WH/WF-1000XM6, WH/WF-1000XM5, and Sony ULT WEAR (WH-ULT900N) are officially compatible. Older models like the WH-1000XM4 lack the necessary hardware, and Apple AirPods are incompatible due to proprietary protocols.

Once set up, your in-game camera responds to your head movements, offering a new level of immersion for race and flight simulators. While not a VR replacement, it provides a free alternative to dedicated tracking setups.

The creator has successfully tested the app with popular titles such as Microsoft Flight Simulator, Elite Dangerous, and Assetto Corsa. Being open-source, the "Sony Head Tracker" is expected to improve and expand its compatibility over time.

headline_marked: [[Anthropic to split Claude subscription billing]] in June 2026, raising costs for agent users
headline: Anthropic to split Claude subscription billing in June 2026, raising costs for agent users
summary: Anthropic announced a new billing system for Claude subscriptions, effective June 2026, which will separate usage for first-party tools from third-party agent/SDK use. This introduces a limited 'Agent SDK credit' that will push heavy users to full API rates.
details: Anthropic's recent changes to Claude's API and subscription policies are diminishing its value for developers, particularly when compared to increasingly competitive open-source models. Users report issues with vendor lock-in and significant price increases.

Claude's API is known for instability, yet it is the only API compatible with a Claude subscription. Other major providers like Vertex AI, AWS Bedrock, and Azure only offer pricier Anthropic API credits, forcing subscribers to rely solely on Anthropic's servers.

Claude Code, Anthropic's primary consumer-facing engineering interface, also faces criticism. Despite being backed by a major company, its CLI has over 9100 open GitHub issues, including long-standing bugs like freezing and screen flickering.

Anthropic announced a significant change to its Claude subscription billing, set to take effect on June 15, 2026. The new system will split usage into two distinct pools: one for Anthropic's first-party tools and another for third-party agent and SDK usage.

Under the new policy, third-party usage will no longer draw from main Claude Pro or Max subscription limits. Instead, it will be covered by a new monthly 'Agent SDK credit' ($20 for Pro, $100 for Max 5x, $200 for Max 20x), after which standard API rates apply.

This change represents a major cost increase for users heavily relying on AI agents. Previously, Claude subscriptions subsidized agent usage at rates 15-30 times cheaper than direct API pricing, a benefit now largely removed.

Even some first-party tools, like `claude -p` within the Claude Code CLI, will draw from 'Extra Usage' and incur charges outside the subscription. Users have reportedly discovered these charges by checking their billing pages rather than through usage limits.
